why: Runtime durable choice revocation cannot use expired setup session, caller bool or caller epoch; it needs genuine current installed actor and one-use trusted human action.

producer.source: Reuse actual root_setup._capture_root_tty_proof/_verify_root_tty_proof, installed root actor/current verified release/MainPID where required, actual active bindings and freshly resolved RootAdoptedSetupChoiceSelection. Observer displays exact purpose/profile/namespace/owner/choice identity/current epoch and asks finite REVOKE action via the genuine foreground root controllingTTY. Retain root-observed response and shown canonical payload digest. No caller-supplied proof/epoch/string confirmation or imported worker input.
producer.constraints: schema1; action literal revoke-adopted-choice; consent_id nullable only non-consent purpose. Exact resolved adopted choice profile/namespace/owner from signed payload/current projection, not caller claims. Registry holds actual actor/TTY proof/PIDFD; one-use <=30s and <=original TTY/actor/current choice deadlines. Revalidate actor/TTY foreground/current owner/policy/key/source choice epoch before consume; never renew old observation.

consumer.constructor: Existing v153 runtime registry injects genuine foreground_tty_observer; no RootBootstrapSession required.
consumer.checks: Root-only lookup/consume genuine observer record, re-resolve exact adopted source row and current epochs/current active owner/source/key before signing. The current root actor is separate from selected worker identity. Root journal serializes competing revoke/config changes atomically; stale observation or changed epoch fails. Sign finite persistent choice-revocation domain through actual AuthorityService public facade; do not import private key methods or mint parallel signer.
consumer.semantics: Exactly one monotonic epoch increment on successful transition, idempotent replay only of same committed consumed observation. Atomic fsync signed revoked row/current index; current adoption/permission immediately denies. Durable revocation has no effect lease and no setup lease extension. Retained owned-process cleanup is independently authorized finite custody cleanup, not arbitrary PID signal.
